stumbles.quote: BioClinical ModernBERT and Clinical ModernBERT both ship Ettin's tokenizer unchanged, so no published clinical ModernBERT has tried a domain token table.
stumbles.why: The "so" conclusion is a stretch. Two models shipping Ettin's tokenizer doesn't show that no published model has tried a domain table. It also assumes the reader knows these models and how they relate to Ettin.

stumbles.quote: A follow-up experiment, `lifesci-ettin`, trains models on it.
stumbles.why: "it" is ambiguous (the token table?), and the experiment is named but not explained or linked. It's also unclear whether it has been run or is only planned.

Ambiguous baseline. It's presumably 21% fewer tokens than the 376 per abstract, but the text never gives the resulting count. Whether the 39,000 training abstracts are disjoint from the 2,000 held-out ones is also not stated.

point: A retrained 50K BPE vocabulary for PubMed text cuts tokens per abstract by 21% versus Ettin's tokenizer if it uses whitespace-only pre-tokenization, but only by 8% if it keeps the GPT-2 pre-tokenizer. This suggests a domain vocabulary can help a lot, though only the token table was tested and not model quality.
